Definition: from a primary κομέω (to tend, i.e. take care of); properly, to provide for, i.e. (by implication) to carry off (as if from harm; genitive case obtain):--bring, receive.
KeyPassages: Matthew 25:27; Luke 7:37; 2 Corinthians 5:10; Ephesians 6:8; Colossians 3:25; Hebrews 10:36
BiblicalUsage: Komizo means to carry off, to receive, to bring back. Matthew 25:27 has the master saying the servant should have put the money to the exchangers, that at his coming he should have received his own with usury, Luke 7:37 has the woman bringing an alabaster box of ointment to Jesus, 2 Corinthians 5:10 says we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that every one may receive the things done in his body, Ephesians 6:8 says whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, Colossians 3:25 says he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong he hath done, and Hebrews 10:36 says after doing the will of God, ye might receive the promise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe receiving is the end of every road in these verses: the servant receives with usury, the worker receives of the Lord, and the patient receive the promise. I hold that the judgment seat of 2 Corinthians 5:10 is where all the receiving is settled, because every man receives according to what he has done.
RelatedBooks: Matthew; Luke; 2 Corinthians; Ephesians; Colossians; Hebrews
